newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia eyes new debt issue after $1 bln global.
newsitem.headline: Colombia eyes new debt issue after $1 bln global.

text.p: Colombia will issue up to $500 million in sovereign debt later this year, in the aftermath of the country's highly successful and first-ever $1 billion global bond deal Thursday, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said.
"We hope to issue between $400 million and $500 million dollars in the second half of the year," Ocampo told reporters.

Ocampo, who spoke after attending a weekly policy meeting of the central bank's board of directors, said the government had still not decided on a market for the new debt issue or whether it should be distributed worldwide like Thursday's deal.
He heralded the global deal as "super successful," however, saying Colombia's investment grade rating had helped it win the lowest interst rate on a global bond ever seen in Latin America.

The central bank had put a $1.4 billion limit on the government's sovereign debt issues in 1997. But Ocampo's comments indicated that agreement had been reached to raise the debt ceiling to $1.5 billion.
